posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Where did the antimatter go? The Big Bang should have created equal amounts of matter and antimatter, which would have annihilated each other instantly. So why does anything exist at all? Scientists are still hunting for the missing half of reality.

What we know about human history is only a fraction of the full story. Much of the rest is like dark matter, invisible to us. We can’t see it, and we can only see the effects of its presence. But thanks to new techniques for DNA sequencing, dating ancient detritus, mathematical models, and aerial and lidar archaeology, we are now able to get a faint idea of what this world might have looked and felt like.

Photographer @sarhaniy has spent years documenting Ta’sheer, a traditional performance practiced in villages around Mecca and Taif.⁠
⁠
During Eid al-Fitr celebrations, weddings, and festivals, young men perform synchronized jumps while firing muzzle-loading rifles downward, creating brief moments of fire and smoke in the air. ⁠
⁠
Their movements require incredible timing, athleticism, and coordination, often performed alongside traditional drums.⁠
⁠
The tradition has been passed down through gen

What if you had 60 seconds to grab anything you wanted from a convenience store, and actually keep it? 😂🇯🇵 ⁠
This is Gigamart Exhibition at Azabudai Hills in Tokyo, where the usual shopping rules get a very fun twist.⁠
⁠
Open for just one month, this Japanese convenience store experience challenges visitors to grab as much as they can in 60 seconds across three areas: the warehouse, back entrance and staff room. ⁠
⁠
🎥: @thetaemarie

You can dive between two continents in Iceland.⁠
⁠
Silfra Fissure in Þingvellir National Park lies between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, making it one of the most unique dive sites in the world.⁠
⁠
The fissure is filled with glacial meltwater filtered through volcanic rock, creating visibility of more than 100 meters.⁠
⁠
The water stays between 2–4°C year-round, so divers wear dry suits while exploring depths of up to 18 meters.⁠
⁠
By: @marina_sixx⁠

Portugal’s most chaotic street musician might just be creating the most unexpectedly beautiful music. 😂🇵🇹🎶⁠
⁠
A street performance featuring a man, a bird, and a whole collection of unexpected sounds that somehow come together into a melody. ⁠
It’s confusing, unpredictable, and oddly mesmerizing, the kind of performance you’d stop walking for just to figure out what’s happening!⁠
⁠
🎥: @cassie.golde

These tiny bats have some very unusual yellow features. 🦇💛⁠
⁠
Honduran white bats have bright yellow ears, noses, and wing membranes because of carotenoid pigments in their skin.⁠
⁠
They get these pigments from their diet, especially the figs they eat. They’re also the first mammals known to have carotenoid pigments in their skin.⁠
⁠
By: @jmneelyphotography

Every opportunity above has a deadline and a selection process. Hotels don’t work like that. They have empty rooms every night and need content constantly, so they’ll host you in exchange for it, no application round required.

The hard part is knowing who to message. We’ve put together 500+ hotels that already host creators, with the decision maker’s name and email for each one and the templates we use to land the stay.

Comment HOTEL and I’ll send it to you.

Would you squeeze through a wooden pillar to receive good fortune? 🍀🇯🇵 ⁠
Inside Tōdai-ji Temple in Nara, Japan, where a wooden pillar in the Great Buddha Hall has a hole said to be the same size as the Great Buddha’s nostril!⁠
⁠
Measuring approximately 37 × 30 cm, the opening is a tight fit, but according to local tradition, those who manage to pass through it are believed to receive good fortune and blessings. ⁠
⁠
Would you dare to give it a try?⁠
🎥: @four.abroad

Only in Shanghai can you find a classroom on one side and a full-on nightclub on the other! 😂🇨🇳⁠
 A place where the vibe switches from studying to partying in what feels like just a few steps. ⁠
⁠
Would you be able to focus knowing the party is happening right next door? 😂⁠
🎥: @mmixiaodou

Thousands of fireflies light up the forests of Valparai every year. ⁠
⁠
From March to May, during the pre-monsoon and early monsoon season, the forests of Valparai in Tamil Nadu come alive with thousands of fireflies. The males flash in synchronized patterns to attract females, creating an incredible natural light show among the trees.⁠
⁠
The humid forests, dense vegetation, and damp soil of the Western Ghats provide ideal conditions for fireflies. But these tiny creatures are facing growing thr

A little reminder that kindness can come from a complete stranger.⁠
@jessicaexploring discovers Ottawa’s “Awesome Box,” a feel-good initiative near the Ottawa Sign in ByWard Market, where people can listen to uplifting messages left by others or record one of their own for someone they’ve never met.⁠
⁠
Sometimes, a few kind words are all it takes to turn someone’s day around.⁠
What message would you leave for a stranger?

These red shapes that appeared above a village in Corsica are called red sprites, and most people have never seen one. ⁠
⁠
Sprites are flashes of light that appear high above powerful thunderstorms, between 40 and 90 km up, and they last only a fraction of a second. ⁠
⁠
To capture these incredible shots, the photographer studied the forecasts and the viewing angle in advance so the sprites would line up with the village. And it worked just perfectly well!⁠
⁠⁠
By: @florian.riou

Ever felt like a city was watching your every move? 👀 ⁠
Sibiu, Romania, where the rooftops have eyes literally!⁠
Look up as you wander through this charming Transylvanian city and you’ll spot rows of windows that look like sleepy or suspicious eyes staring right back at you. 🏘️✨ ⁠
⁠
These distinctive rooftop windows are part of Sibiu’s historic architecture, giving the city an unexpectedly quirky personality.⁠
Would you feel watched or find it fascinating? 👀⁠
🎥: @katarzyna.zabek
